messages:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing missing spans when traffic goes edge-gateway -> async worker -> batch job. Traces look fine end-to-end for direct requests but the async fanout drops the parent context :confused:

dan: Do we have an example trace id where this happens?

maria: 0x4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 — last span stops at gateway, worker starts a new trace. Happening on kafka consumer and SQS retries.

ashley: Sounds like context injection on publish isn't consistent. Some publishers use `traceparent` header + `baggage`, others use a custom `x-rd-trace` header. Mix of formats causes downstream libs to fail to extract.

sara: Can we standardize on W3C tracecontext `traceparent` + `baggage` and use base64 when stuffing into message attributes? Many providers limit header chars.

kevin: Agreed. Also need to carry sampling decision. If gateway decides `sampled=0`, workers shouldn't start sampled spans or send to exporter. We had explosions in retention due to re-sampled async tasks.

maria: Proposal: gateway always injects `traceparent` and `tracestate` when publishing, and additionally `x-rd-sampled` with values `0|1|d` (d=deferred). Consumers must honor `x-rd-sampled` if present.

ashley: Implementation notes: for Kafka use headers (binary safe). For SQS/SNS set message attributes with DataType=String and value base64(traceparent) so we don't hit control-char issues. Example:```
MessageAttributes: {
  traceparent: { DataType: 'String', StringValue: '00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01' },
  x-rd-sampled: { DataType: 'String', StringValue: '1' }
}
```

dan: For batched jobs (consumer reads N messages) we should attach each message's trace as its own child span OR create a fan-in span that references all trace ids? Mixing both is messy. I'd prefer one root span per message to keep timelines clear.

kevin: Also watch out for size limits on SQS attributes and Kafka header counts. We should keep `tracestate` trimmed (only include origin=redwood plus sampling flag). Full baggage can be stored in the payload under `__rd_baggage` if needed.

ashley: +1. SDK changes: add helpers `inject_message_context(msg, channel)` and `extract_message_context(msg)` that unify across transports. Put in infra-libs repo and use CI lint to forbid ad-hoc header names.

maria: Ops ask: when a consumer restarts and reprocesses, we sometimes generate duplicate trace ids (bad). Ensure we never regenerate parent trace id on retries; instead continue with same traceparent from message attributes.

infra-bot: deploy:infra-libs v0.24.0 pushed to canary with new `inject_message_context` helpers :rocket:

dan: I'll run a canary on kafka-consumers and SQS-workers. If we see <1% context-loss after roll, we can standardize.

sara: One more: exporter retention. If sampling==0 we should drop spans early. For sampled==d (deferred), the gateway can set `x-rd-sampled=d` and downstream may decide to record minimal traces (span count limited) until a decision is made. That prevents quota spikes.

kevin: Let's document the spec in platform/telemetry (including examples for Kafka, SQS, Redis lists). I'll create a short RFC and link tests to preserve format.

maria: Thanks — big win if we can get consistent trace handoff across gateways and async.

ashley: FYI I added unit tests that simulate truncation and ensure consumers still parse `traceparent` when base64-encoded.

dan: Tracking: #telemetry-ctx-propagation in trackers. Will post canary results tomorrow. :eyes:
